original_question: Is the problem of recognizing whether a graph is the visibility graph of a simple polygon in NP?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1 (Visibility Graph Recognition), Open Problem 29, read together with the immediately preceding definition of the polygon visibility-graph recognition problem and Open Problem 28.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right complexity-theoretic focus (membership in NP), the right object class (graphs arising from simple polygons), and the right task (recognition rather than reconstruction or characterization). It is very close to the paper's actual open problem.
missing_details: Specify that 'visibility graph' here means the vertex visibility graph of a simple polygon, not the point, segment, bar, or rectangle visibility graphs discussed elsewhere in the survey.

State the underlying decision problem explicitly: the input is a graph G (officially, in adjacency-matrix form), and the question is whether there exists a simple polygon P whose visibility graph is exactly G.

Include the paper's visibility convention from Section 1: two polygon vertices are adjacent exactly when the segment joining them lies entirely within P; this convention allows the segment to graze along a polygon edge or pass through a reflex vertex.
Clarify that the question is about membership in the class NP for the general recognition problem, not about NP-hardness or NP-completeness.

Make clear that this is the unrestricted recognition problem, not the easier variant where a Hamiltonian cycle corresponding to the polygon boundary is given as part of the input (that is a separate Open Problem 30).
refined_question: Given a finite graph G in adjacency-matrix form, consider the decision problem of determining whether there exists a simple polygon P in the plane such that the vertices of G are in bijection with the vertices of P and two vertices of G are adjacent if and only if the line segment joining the corresponding vertices of P lies entirely within P (with visibility interpreted as in the paper, so the segment may graze a polygon edge or pass through a reflex vertex). Does this recognition problem for vertex visibility graphs of simple polygons belong to NP?
justification: The exact target is Open Problem 29 in Section 4.1. Your draft is nearly verbatim, but the paper uses 'visibility graph' for several different geometric models across points, segments, bars, rectangles, and polygons, so the polygonal meaning must be made explicit. The immediately preceding paragraph in Section 4.1 defines the relevant recognition problem for simple polygons, Open Problem 28 spells out the underlying existence question for a graph G, and Section 1 provides the visibility convention for polygon vertices. Open Problem 30 shows that the paper treats the boundary-cycle-given variant separately, so the refined question should stay with the general recognition problem and should not add that extra promise.
